messages.content:
You answer questions for an engineering team from a memory store. The user message holds the memory you may use, then the question.
Rules:
- Answer only from the memory provided. Do not use outside knowledge and do not guess.
- If the memory does not contain the answer, reply exactly: I don't know
- When the memory does contain it, reply in one short line with just the value asked for (a name, a team, a service, a date, a note label, a reason) and nothing else.
- When a value changed over time, answer for the moment the question asks about; without a stated moment, answer for now. Today is 2026-06-30.
- Memory entries carry the date they were recorded. Treat a later entry as superseding an earlier one on the same subject.

Memory:
- [2026-03-02] standup/ember/2026-03-02: Reminder from the Ember team: page Oskar Lind for anything this cycle, not Diego.
- [2026-03-03] standup/cinder/2026-03-03: The auth gateway deploy window (unchanged): on Mondays between 10:00 and 12:00 UTC.
- [2026-03-09] handover/2026-03-09-feature-flags-correction: Correction to the handover note of 2026-02-11: the flags service went to team Atlas, not Dune. Dune never owned it; the note was written against the wrong team.
- [2026-03-11] standup/dune/2026-03-11: Tomasz has the Dune pager this cycle, taking over from Farah.
- [2026-03-11] standup/cinder/2026-03-11: No deploys to Ledger from 2026-03-30 to 2026-04-03 because of the fiscal year close.
- [2026-03-11] standup/cinder/2026-03-11-2: The Cinder team noticed that billing-api's cold start time tripled after the runtime upgrade and pinged the owners.
- [2026-03-17] standup/atlas/2026-03-17: Decided in today's standup: image-resizer will keep original uploads for 90 days only, since storage for originals doubled in six months. For anything Atlas-related, page Priya.
- [2026-03-20] standup/boreal/2026-03-20: Marcus moves from team Boreal to the Atlas team today. On-call for Boreal passes from Marcus to Lena with the move.
- [2026-03-20] standup/boreal/2026-03-20-2: Observation from the Boreal team: after the retention change, the catalog service's disk usage jumped 30 percent. The Boreal team runs its planning on Thursdays.
- [2026-03-20] standup/atlas/2026-03-20: Priya runs the quarterly capacity review.
- [2026-04-01] handover/2026-04-01-search-indexer: From today the pager for the search indexer rings the Boreal team, not team Atlas. Ownership transferred.
- [2026-04-03] standup/cinder/2026-04-03: Cinder runs its planning on Mondays.
- [2026-04-08] standup/atlas/2026-04-08: Reminder from the Atlas team: page Marcus for anything this cycle, not Priya. The Atlas team saw that webhooks' request volume halved following the client rollout; not their service, so they flagged it.
- [2026-04-13] standup/ember/2026-04-13: Diego has the Ember pager this cycle, taking over from Oskar.
- [2026-04-13] standup/ember/2026-04-13-2: Ember still owns the reporting service, in case anyone asks.
- [2026-04-14] standup/dune/2026-04-14: Rotation day for the Dune team: Tomasz hands the pager to Farah.
- [2026-04-14] standup/dune/2026-04-14-2: The Dune team noticed that the reporting service's p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy and pinged the owners.
- [2026-04-14] standup/dune/2026-04-14-3: Release captain for Q3 2025: Farah.
- [2026-04-16] standup/atlas/2026-04-16: The Atlas team saw that the ledger service's disk usage jumped 30 percent following the retention change; not their service, so they flagged it.
- [2026-05-19] incident-review/INC-2026-009: Incident review INC-2026-009. The scheduler ran the nightly jobs twice on 2026-05-16. Root cause: two leaders elected during a network partition. Decision: the scheduler leader lease will be shortened to ten seconds, because two leaders ran the nightly jobs twice in INC-2026-009.
- [2026-05-22] standup/dune/2026-05-22: Tomasz picked up the Dune on-call shift from Farah today.
- [2026-05-22] standup/dune/2026-05-22-2: The Dune team noticed that auth-gateway's CPU sat at 90 percent after the traffic shift and pinged the owners.
- [2026-05-22] standup/dune/2026-05-22-3: Heads-up from the Dune team: the scheduler's error rate crept up to 2 percent after the dependency bump.
- [2026-05-22] standup/dune/2026-05-22-4: The Dune team planning meeting is every Wednesday.
- [2026-05-27] standup/atlas/2026-05-27: Decided in today's standup: the event-bus will retain messages for seven days, since replaying a full week has covered every incident recovery so far. The Atlas team noticed that search-indexer's p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy and pinged the owners. The catalog still relies on the resizer; keep that in mind for the maintenance.
- [2026-05-28] standup/ember/2026-05-28: Ember noticed that the ledger service's p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy and pinged the owners.
- [2026-05-29] standup/ember/2026-05-29: On-call rotation: Oskar is primary for team Ember starting today; Diego is off rotation.
- [2026-06-01] standup/ember/2026-06-01: For newcomers: the deploy window for the reporting service is still on Tuesdays and Thursdays between 10:00 and 12:00 UTC.
- [2026-06-04] standup/atlas/2026-06-04: Priya Raman has the Atlas pager this cycle, taking over from Marcus.
- [2026-06-04] standup/boreal/2026-06-04: Boreal noticed that the catalog service's memory use grew steadily for a week after the cache change and pinged the owners.
- [2026-06-09] standup/dune/2026-06-09: Observation from team Dune: after the retention change, search-indexer's disk usage jumped 30 percent.

Question: Which team owned reporting before Dune?

message.reasoning:
The question asks which team owned reporting before Dune. Let me look through the memory.

Memory entries about reporting:
- 2026-04-13: "Ember still owns the reporting service, in case anyone asks."
- 2026-04-14: "The Dune team noticed that the reporting service's p99 latency doubled after Tuesday's deploy and pinged the owners."

There's no entry saying Dune owned reporting or that ownership transferred from anyone to Dune. The question presupposes Dune owned reporting at some point. The memory doesn't contain that. There's no mention of reporting ownership transferring to Dune.

So the answer based on memory: Ember owns the reporting service. But the question asks "before Dune" — the memory never says Dune owned reporting. Actually, per memory, Ember owns reporting (as of 2026-04-13), and Dune pinged the owners (not Dune itself). So the premise is false; memory doesn't say Dune owned it. Should I answer "I don't know" or "Ember"?

The rules: "If the memory does not contain the answer, reply exactly: I don't know." The question asks which team owned reporting before Dune. Memory doesn't state Dune ever owned reporting; it states Ember owns it. The presupposition that Dune owned it isn't supported. So the strict answer is "I don't know."

Hmm, but one could argue the answer is Ember — Dune noticed reporting's p99 doubled and "pinged the owners," implying Dune isn't the owner. And Ember still owns reporting. So if the question assumes Dune owned reporting before someone... The question: "Which team owned reporting before Dune?" That implies ownership sequence: X → Dune. Memory says Ember owns it; Dune is not the owner. So the question's premise conflicts with memory.

The safest answer per rules: the memory does not contain which team owned reporting before Dune (no such transfer recorded). So "I don't know."

Alternatively, one might interpret: maybe the question intends the current owner before considering a mistaken belief that Dune owns it. But strict rule-following: answer only from memory; memory says Ember owns reporting. The question "before Dune" — there's no record of Dune owning reporting. So I don't know.
